title: Successive Phase Transitions from a Composite Fermion Liquid to a Fractional Quantum Hall State at ν=3/2 Driven by In-Plane Magnetic Field
authors: Xinghao Wang, L. N. Pfeiffer, A. Gupta, K. W. Baldwin, K. W. West, Rui-Rui Du
abstract: We report an even-denominator fractional quantum Hall state at ν = 3/2 induced entirely by in-plane magnetic field B_|| in an ultra-high-mobility GaAs quantum well. As B_|| increases, the system undergoes two successive transitions: from a composite fermion liquid to a soft-gap FQH state (B_||~12.2 T), then via a topological phase transition to a hard-gap robust FQH state (B_||~14.7 T), accompanied by a daughter state at ν = 19/13. We present systematic data, and discuss a possible scenario in interpreting these findings. Our work demonstrates that topological order may be engineered through k-space Fermi contour splitting under an in-plane magnetic field.
summary: This work reports on the observation of successive phase transitions in a $\nu=3/2$ Fractional Quantum Hall state within a GaAs quantum well, driven solely by an in-plane magnetic field. The system transitions from a Composite Fermion liquid through a soft-gap state to a robust, hard-gap FQH state. This demonstrates that topological order can be engineered by manipulating the electron's k-space Fermi contour using external magnetic fields.
main_problem: The study investigates the successive phase transitions occurring in a Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) state at filling fraction $\nu=3/2$ when driven by an in-plane magnetic field ($B_{\parallel}$).
main_result: The system undergoes two distinct transitions: from a Composite Fermion (CF) liquid to a soft-gap FQH state, followed by a transition to a hard-gap, robust FQH state, accompanied by a daughter state at $\nu=19/13$.
method: Measurements of magnetoresistance ($R_{xx}$) and Hall resistance ($R_{xy}$) are performed on an ultra-high-mobility GaAs quantum well by varying the in-plane magnetic field and tilt angle.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in a GaAs quantum well, exhibiting correlated electron behavior characteristic of the Fractional Quantum Hall Effect. The theoretical framework involves composite fermion theory and analyzing the splitting of the Fermi contour in k-space.
key_observables: FQH plateaus, resistance jumps, gap energy ($\Delta''$), and the evolution of $R_{xx}$ and $R_{xy}$ as a function of $B_{\parallel}$.
important_parameters: Filling factor $\nu=3/2$, in-plane magnetic field $B_{\parallel}$ (transition points at $\sim 12.2$ T and $\sim 14.7$ T), and the tilt angle $\theta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the in-plane field causes a k-space Fermi contour splitting, driving the transition from a CF liquid to a topologically distinct FQH state.
figures_summary: Figures detail the evolution of $R_{xx}$ and $R_{xy}$ with tilt angle and $B_{\parallel}$, specifically highlighting the two transition points at $\nu=3/2$ and the associated daughter state at $\nu=19/13$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents data showing the initial CF liquid state, followed by the first transition to a soft-gap FQH state, and finally the second transition to a hard-gap, robust FQH state, supported by gap measurements and theoretical interpretations of the k-space physics.
why_interesting: The observation of field-induced topological transitions in a highly correlated electron system like the FQH state provides a clean experimental platform to study how external fields can engineer topological order, which has implications for understanding exotic quantum states.
